assessment.nobel_worthiness: Incretin physiology and GLP-1-based therapy form a clear arc from hormone biology to drugs that change the treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity. The scientific originality (proglucagon processing, GLP-1 as an insulinotropic and satiety signal) and the scale of clinical and public-health impact are both exceptional and unambiguous.
assessment.attribution: Drucker (GLP-1 biology and receptor physiology) and Holst (identification and characterization of the active gut hormone in humans) are the clearest scientific contributors. Knudsen represents the pharmacological step that produced durable long-acting agonists. Mojsov's sequence and structure contribution is real but its weight relative to others is disputed, so I leave her out of this configuration while acknowledging that the credit question is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent physiological confirmation, large randomized outcome trials and broad global use make this mature; recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Fair allocation of credit among the several discoverers of the active peptide and the drug developers is contested.
Whether the committee prefers a physiology-only or a physiology-plus-drug-development configuration is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically targeted light control of defined cell types transformed circuit neuroscience, letting investigators test causality in identified neuron populations in behaving animals. It is an enabling invention of broad and lasting scientific impact, and is widely used for dissecting motor, sensory and cognitive circuits.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann identified and characterized channelrhodopsin as a light-gated channel; Deisseroth led the demonstration and deployment in neurons and in vivo. Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck made important contributions, so the three-person limit forces a difficult and contestable choice; I choose the people whose roles I regard as most decisive for the core discovery and its generalization.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and independently confirmed across thousands of laboratories; the tool is long established. Therapeutic translation (for example, vision restoration) is early but not required for recognition.
uncertainties: The attribution among six credited people is contested and a three-person cap cannot reflect every key contributor.
Priority disputes concerning who first expressed channelrhodopsin in neurons for control of activity may matter.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineering patient T cells with chimeric antigen receptors established a new class of living drug with durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies. The conceptual originality and clinical impact are very high and the field has opened a new therapeutic modality.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain and June led the construction and clinical translation of second-generation CAR-T cells; Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell transfer and early clinical gene-engineered T-cell therapy. Other early inventors (for example, those who first designed chimeric receptors) are not on the supplied list, so the credit configuration rests on this set.
assessment.maturity: Approved products, years of follow-up and multiple independent groups confirming efficacy make this mature, though long-term safety and application in solid tumors remain open.
uncertainties: Early chimeric-receptor inventors outside the supplied credit list may deserve consideration; I cannot verify their absence from the longlist.
Efficacy is established in hematologic cancers but not generally in solid tumors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orexin/hypocretin links a discrete hypothalamic neuropeptide system to the stability of wakefulness and to the mechanism of narcolepsy type 1. The work gave a cellular and molecular explanation of a sleep disorder and has led to orexin receptor drugs for sleep disorders. It is a clear and well-defined circuit-level discovery.
assessment.attribution: Yanagisawa and Sakurai identified orexin peptides and receptors and showed the narcolepsy phenotype in knockout mice; Mignot positionally cloned the canine narcolepsy gene (the orexin receptor 2) and linked the human disease to orexin deficiency. de Lecea and Kilduff's near-simultaneous hypocretin discovery creates a priority question, which complicates a clean three-person configuration.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed across species and in human neuropathology; therapeutics (orexin antagonists, agonists in development) are arriving, so timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: The simultaneous discovery of hypocretin and orexin by two groups creates a credit and naming dispute.
Orexin agonist therapies for narcolepsy are still in clinical development.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Positional cloning of leptin revealed an adipose-derived hormone signalling energy stores to the hypothalamus, founding the endocrine and neural understanding of body-weight regulation. The discovery is original, clear and conceptually foundational for energy homeostasis, with direct therapeutic relevance in leptin-deficient states.
assessment.attribution: Friedman is the credited cloner of the leptin gene and the clean single credit supplied. Prior parabiosis work by Douglas Coleman is not in the credited list and the longlist cannot resolve how that precursor would be recognized; I treat the single-name configuration as possible but incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Highly confirmed for more than three decades; recognition could be seen as timely, though the incretin field has more recently eclipsed it in clinical impact.
uncertainties: Coleman's earlier contribution cannot be recognized posthumously, and a single-laureate prize may be seen as incomplete.
Limited therapeutic reach of leptin itself in common obesity could reduce its relative standing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing that blocking a single cytokine, TNF, controls rheumatoid arthritis was a proof of principle that reshaped treatment of chronic inflammatory disease and established the biologics era. The impact on patient outcomes and on the cytokine-targeting concept is large and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini led the mechanistic rationale and the first clinical proof in rheumatoid arthritis, a coherent two-person configuration. The antibody engineering and drug development by others (not on this list) is a separate contribution.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with decades of clinical use and several approved agents; recognition would be late rather than premature.
uncertainties: Possible competing claims from antibody engineers and from earlier TNF biology researchers outside the supplied credit list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-term potentiation provided the first widely accepted cellular and synaptic model for how experience-dependent plasticity can store information, and it organizes a vast literature on learning and memory. The foundational observation and its mechanistic follow-up (NMDA receptor dependence) are of lasting importance in synaptic physiology.
assessment.attribution: Bliss and Lømo made the original discovery of LTP in the hippocampus; Collingridge established NMDA receptor dependence as its mechanism. Morris linked it to behavior and spatial learning through pharmacological block, a significant but more indirect contribution. This is a realistic but debatable three-person choice.
assessment.maturity: Very mature and independently confirmed; some uncertainty remains about the degree to which LTP maps onto memory storage in vivo, but the phenomenon itself is firmly established.
uncertainties: Causal links between LTP and memory remain debated.
The choice between Collingridge and Morris for a three-person limit is not clear cut.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway identified how cytosolic DNA is sensed and converted into innate immune signalling through the second messenger cGAMP. It is a mechanistically clear pathway with broad relevance to infection, autoimmunity, senescence and cancer immunity, and it links molecular biochemistry to disease.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the cGAMP second messenger; Barber identified STING. Ishikawa, Wu and Sun were important co-authors, but the decisive conceptual contributions appear to rest with Chen and Barber, based on the supplied credit and my own recollection, which I have not independently verified.
assessment.maturity: The pathway is well confirmed biochemically and genetically, but therapeutic translation (STING agonists and inhibitors) has not yet produced approved drugs, so the clinical relevance remains partly prospective.
uncertainties: Clinical efficacy of STING-targeted therapies is unproven.
Prior work on cyclic dinucleotide signalling in bacteria and the contributions of other groups may complicate attribution.
